title: Create a test S3 bucket and turn on versioning

content.goal: Create a test Amazon S3 bucket, turn on versioning, upload test files, and prove that S3 keeps older versions after changes or deletes.
content.title: Create a test S3 bucket and turn on versioning

cleanup.text: Delete all stored object versions from the bucket.
Delete all delete markers from the bucket.
Delete the test bucket and remove local notes.txt file.

cliSteps.note: Requires AWS CLI v2 configured with active credentials.
cliSteps.title: Set shell variables

commands.text:
REGION="eu-west-2"
PROFILE="default"
ACCOUNT_ID=$(aws sts get-caller-identity --profile "$PROFILE" --query Account --output text)
BUCKET="s3-task-2-versioning-$ACCOUNT_ID"

echo "Bucket: $BUCKET"
echo "Region: $REGION"

cliSteps.expectedResult: Shell prints bucket name containing your AWS account ID.

cliSteps.note: LocationConstraint is required for regions outside us-east-1.
cliSteps.title: Create the test bucket
Enable versioning
cliSteps.expectedResult: Command completes silently with exit code 0.

cliSteps.title: Upload version 1

commands.text:
echo "version 1" > notes.txt

aws s3api put-object \
  --bucket "$BUCKET" \
  --key notes.txt \
  --body notes.txt \
  --profile "$PROFILE"

cliSteps.expectedResult: Returns ETag and VersionId for the first version.

cliSteps.note: Same key (notes.txt). New content produces a new VersionId.
cliSteps.title: Upload version 2

commands.text:
echo "version 2" > notes.txt

aws s3api put-object \
  --bucket "$BUCKET" \
  --key notes.txt \
  --body notes.txt \
  --profile "$PROFILE"

cliSteps.title: List object versions
cliSteps.expectedResult: JSON response lists two object entries under Versions array.

cliSteps.title: Delete object and view delete marker

commands.text:
aws s3api delete-object \
  --bucket "$BUCKET" \
  --key notes.txt \
  --profile "$PROFILE"

aws s3api list-object-versions \
  --bucket "$BUCKET" \
  --prefix notes.txt \
  --profile "$PROFILE"

cliSteps.expectedResult: JSON lists a DeleteMarker entry alongside previous Versions.

cliSteps.title: Tear down all versions and the bucket
cliSteps.warning: This command permanently removes object versions, delete markers, and the bucket.

commands.text:
aws s3api delete-objects \
  --bucket "$BUCKET" \
  --delete "$(aws s3api list-object-versions \
    --bucket "$BUCKET" \
    --query '{Objects: Versions[].{Key:Key,VersionId:VersionId}}' \
    --output json \
    --profile "$PROFILE")" \
  --profile "$PROFILE" 2>/dev/null || true

aws s3api delete-objects \
  --bucket "$BUCKET" \
  --delete "$(aws s3api list-object-versions \
    --bucket "$BUCKET" \
    --query '{Objects: DeleteMarkers[].{Key:Key,VersionId:VersionId}}' \
    --output json \
    --profile "$PROFILE")" \
  --profile "$PROFILE" 2>/dev/null || true

aws s3 rb "s3://$BUCKET" --profile "$PROFILE"
rm -f notes.txt

cliSteps.expectedResult: Bucket and local test file are removed cleanly.

concepts.body: Amazon S3 can keep multiple versions of the same object key in the same bucket.
concepts.title: Versioning

concepts.body: The object key is the file path/name inside the bucket, such as notes.txt.
concepts.title: Object key

concepts.body: Uploading a file with an existing key creates a new version instead of permanently overwriting the old version.
concepts.title: Overwrite behavior

concepts.body: Deleting a versioned object adds a delete marker. Older versions still exist and can be restored.
concepts.title: Delete marker

concepts.body: After enabling versioning, you can only suspend it. You cannot return the bucket to the unversioned state.
concepts.title: Versioning cannot be disabled

concepts.body: Each stored version incurs standard storage charges. Old versions are real stored objects.
concepts.title: Cost reminder

examTips.text: SAA-C03: Select S3 Versioning when a question requires protection against accidental object overwrite or deletion.
SAA-C03: S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) and Same-Region Replication (SRR) both strictly require Versioning to be enabled on source and destination buckets.
SAA-C03: Pair S3 Versioning with Lifecycle rules to transition noncurrent object versions to S3 Glacier for cost optimization.

examTraps.body: Versioning protects from accidental overwrite/delete, but doesn't protect against bucket deletion or account compromise unless paired with MFA Delete and S3 Replication.
examTraps.title: Versioning is not a complete backup by itself

examTraps.body: A normal delete merely adds a delete marker. Older object versions remain in storage and continue to incur charges until explicitly deleted.
examTraps.title: Deleting a versioned object does NOT free storage space immediately

examTraps.body: Once enabled, S3 versioning can only be Suspended. Suspending stops creating new versions for new uploads, but retains existing version history.
examTraps.title: Versioning cannot be disabled

examTraps.body: MFA Delete requires root account credentials to enable and adds extra protection for deleting object versions or changing bucket versioning state.
examTraps.title: MFA Delete is separate from basic versioning

cheatSheet.body: Keeps multiple versions of an object in one bucket to protect against accidental overwrite or delete.
cheatSheet.title: S3 Versioning

cheatSheet.body: Uploading to an existing key creates a new version rather than replacing the old object permanently.
cheatSheet.title: Overwrite protection

cheatSheet.body: A standard delete inserts a delete marker as the current version instead of deleting old versions.
cheatSheet.title: Delete marker

cheatSheet.body: Once versioning is enabled, it can be suspended, but cannot be reverted to unversioned.
cheatSheet.title: Suspend only

cheatSheet.body: All stored versions count toward S3 storage charges until deleted or expired by lifecycle rules.
cheatSheet.title: Storage Cost

cheatSheet.body: All object versions and delete markers must be deleted before S3 permits bucket deletion.
cheatSheet.title: Bucket Deletion

content.memoryHook: S3 versioning is a save-history button. Overwrite creates a new save. Delete adds a marker. Old saves remain recoverable.
content.costWarning: This lab costs minimal amounts if tiny test files are used and resources are torn down promptly. S3 charges apply to object storage, API requests, and non-current versions. Delete all versions and delete markers during cleanup.

consoleSteps.title: Start from AWS login

instructions.text: Sign in to the AWS Management Console.
Use an admin user or lab role with S3 permissions.
Use the Region eu-west-2 (Europe London) for this lab.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Signed into the AWS Management Console in Region eu-west-2.

consoleSteps.note: S3 bucket names are globally unique across all AWS accounts. Appending your account ID prevents naming collisions.
consoleSteps.title: Create the S3 bucket

instructions.text: Open Amazon S3 from the Console service menu.
Click Create bucket.
Enter Bucket name: s3-task-2-versioning-[account-id] (replace [account-id] with your real AWS account ID or unique string).
Select AWS Region: Europe (London) eu-west-2.
Keep Block all public access enabled.
Click Create bucket at the bottom of the page.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The bucket appears in your Amazon S3 bucket list.

consoleSteps.title: Turn on bucket versioning
consoleSteps.warning: Once versioning is enabled on a bucket, it can be suspended later, but cannot be returned to the unversioned state.

instructions.text: Click on your new bucket name to open it.
Select the Properties tab.
Locate the Bucket Versioning panel.
Click Edit.
Select Enable.
Click Save changes.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Bucket Versioning status displays Enabled under Properties.

consoleSteps.title: Upload the first test file

instructions.text: Create a small text file on your local machine named notes.txt.
Add simple text inside the file: version 1.
In the bucket Objects tab, click Upload.
Add notes.txt and click Upload.
Confirm notes.txt appears in the object list.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: notes.txt is uploaded successfully to the root of the bucket.

consoleSteps.note: Because versioning is enabled, S3 stores the new content as a separate version while preserving the previous version.
consoleSteps.title: Upload a changed version

instructions.text: Edit local notes.txt file to change its content to: version 2.
Upload the modified notes.txt to the exact same S3 bucket.
Keep the object key identical (notes.txt).
Confirm the upload completes.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The upload succeeds without deleting the previous version.

consoleSteps.note: This confirms versioning is functioning correctly.
consoleSteps.title: Show object versions

instructions.text: In the S3 bucket object list, toggle on Show versions.
Locate notes.txt.
Verify that two versions of notes.txt are listed.
Note that each version has a distinct Version ID.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Two versions of notes.txt are displayed under the object hierarchy.

consoleSteps.title: Delete the object and view the delete marker
consoleSteps.warning: A standard delete on a versioned object inserts a delete marker. It does not permanently remove older versions.

instructions.text: Select notes.txt and click Delete.
Confirm deletion by typing delete.
Ensure Show versions remains enabled.
Observe the Delete marker listed at the top of the version stack.
Confirm older versions still exist beneath the delete marker.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: A Delete marker is created as the current version; earlier versions remain intact.

consoleSteps.title: Verify the lab

instructions.text: Confirm Bucket versioning status is Enabled.
Confirm notes.txt has multiple historical versions.
Confirm deleting the object placed a Delete marker.
Confirm older versions are visible when Show versions is on.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: All lab verification criteria are satisfied.

consoleSteps.title: Tear down in the correct order
consoleSteps.warning: All object versions and delete markers must be permanently deleted before S3 allows a versioned bucket to be deleted.

instructions.text: Open the S3 bucket with Show versions turned ON.
Select all versions of notes.txt and click Delete.
Select all delete markers and click Delete.
Confirm permanently delete for all selected versions.
Verify the bucket is completely empty.
Delete the test bucket.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Bucket is permanently deleted and no residual AWS resources remain.

verification.text: Uploading the same object key twice creates two distinct object versions.
Deleting the object creates a delete marker while older versions remain accessible.

content.whyItMatters: Amazon S3 versioning protects against accidental overwrites and deletes. It is a fundamental building block for backup, recovery, and secure object storage design.

troubleshooting.body: S3 bucket names are globally unique across all AWS accounts. Append your account ID or a random string.
troubleshooting.title: Bucket name already exists

troubleshooting.body: Refresh the Console Properties tab or execute get-bucket-versioning via AWS CLI.
troubleshooting.title: Versioning status does not show Enabled

troubleshooting.body: Ensure the Show versions toggle is switched ON in the S3 bucket object browser.
troubleshooting.title: Only one version appears in Console

troubleshooting.body: Delete every version of every object and all delete markers before attempting bucket deletion.
troubleshooting.title: Bucket deletion fails with BucketNotEmpty error

troubleshooting.body: Ensure your AWS IAM user or role has s3:CreateBucket, s3:PutBucketVersioning, s3:PutObject, s3:GetObjectVersion, and s3:DeleteObject permissions.
troubleshooting.title: CLI permission denied

troubleshooting.body: Ensure LocationConstraint matches your specified --region parameter (e.g. eu-west-2).
troubleshooting.title: InvalidLocationConstraint CLI error
